items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for the reaction of methane with bromine in bright light.

rubric.why: Chlorine substitutes for one hydrogen atom in methane, producing chloromethane and hydrogen chloride.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct balanced equation.

rubric.why: Bright light is the condition for the substitution reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying that the reaction takes place in bright light or sunlight.

modelAnswer: The reaction takes place in bright light.

items.followUp: State two conclusions about the atom drawn from Rutherford’s gold-foil experiment.

accept: most of the atom is empty
rubric.why: Most of the volume of an atom is empty space.
rubric.description: State that most of the atom is empty space.

rubric.why: The nucleus occupies a very small region at the centre of the atom.
rubric.description: Identify the nucleus as very small and central.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the nucleus as small and central.

accept: positive charge concentrated in the nucleus
rubric.why: The atom’s positive charge is concentrated in its nucleus.
rubric.description: State that the nucleus is positively charged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the positive charge in the nucleus.

rubric.why: Nearly all the mass of the atom is concentrated in the nucleus.
rubric.description: State that most of the atom’s mass is in the nucleus.

rubric.why: In Rutherford’s model, electrons move around the nucleus.
rubric.description: State that electrons revolve around the nucleus.

modelAnswer: Most of the volume of an atom is empty space.
At the centre of the atom is a very small, dense nucleus.
The nucleus is positively charged and contains nearly all the mass of the atom.
The atom is electrically neutral overall because its positive and negative charges balance.
